findings.quoted_finding: B.8 treats x^h as an unsupported deviation without proving the same bound when it is a zero-mass support point.
defect_evidence: The proof asserts that the off-support proposal x^h guarantees z_H while the maintained Borel laws permit x^h to lie in topological support with zero mass.
mechanical_checks: Read exact original B.8 and E.3 at SHA6708eaaf; checked the common-value and high-type rejection premises.
findings.reasoning: The stated shortcut does not cover every feasible assessment. A local-Bayes argument repairs it: for V<z_H, a small ball has x_H>V, cannot carry used zero-posterior mass by either payoff branch, and hence has posterior above p* almost surely. The local Bayes limit at a supported x^h is at least p* and admissibility forces it above p*. Then x^h pays z_H, a contradiction. Off support, the specified high posterior yields the same deviation. No primitive or equilibrium domain is changed.
findings.disposition: Write and review an explicit lemma in the new notes, and prepare a pure B.8 repair patch. Preserve the original source and all v1 files.
